passage.title: Original practice poem 'Allotment, October', written for Tarbiyyah Global Academy
paras: The bean poles lean together now,
like old friends with nothing left to say.
The last tomatoes split their skins;
a robin argues with the rain.
My grandfather turns the soil, slowly,
folding summer under like a letter
Next spring, he says, the ground remembers.
I look at the bare brown rows
the way he believes the seed.

questions.q: Step 2: who speaks, about what, and what changes?
questions.a: a grandchild watching the grandfather prepare the allotment for winter; from ending to hope
questions.model: I do: speaker: 'my grandfather' shows a grandchild; subject: the autumn allotment; change: from tired ending to belief in spring.

questions.q: Annotate 'a robin argues with the rain': method and effect
questions.a: personification; the garden is still lively and defiant

questions.q: in the portal response box, write two analytical paragraphs on how the poet presents change. Starter: 'The poet presents change as...'
questions.a: Two paragraphs: method, short quotation, effect
questions.model: Point: change is presented as tiredness at first | Evidence: 'like old friends with nothing left to say' | Method: simile | Effect: the season feels worn out, gentle rather than harsh

questions.q: write a paragraph on the final stanza's shift in tone
comment on the form: three equal stanzas and the effect of the last line
questions.a: A comment on form and the ending
